windowTitle: Serial integration stage 6 - default App Console delivery view

necessity.decision: The two supported delivery combinations are the default App (an approved Runtime Release with built-in UI, no Package/Build/CapabilityVersion) and the Agent (Package + Runtime + independent WebUI). The Console delivery view is the surface that renders that chain. It must render both combinations; today it fails the default App entirely. This change makes it render the default App, changing no other behavior.
necessity.currentProblem: apps/console-bff/internal/httpapi/delivery.go returned `serve: deployment <id> names no capability version` whenever the current deployment and the Workspace both named no capability version. A default-App deployment is exactly that case, so `GET /api/v2/delivery/{workspaceId}` answered an owner-read failure (502) for every default-App Workspace, and the Console Workspace delivery panel showed `delivery_unavailable` instead of the chain. This contradicts the adopted delivery invariant that the default App needs no synthetic Package, Build or CapabilityVersion.
confirmedFacts: services/serve/internal/delivery/write.go stores a default-App reservation/deployment with an empty capability_version_id and a runtime selection, while the Agent path stores a capability_version_id.

docs/invariants.md Adopted Application Delivery Invariants: the default App uses an exact approved Runtime Release and needs no synthetic Package, Build or CapabilityVersion; the Agent uses Build with exact Package, Runtime and independent WebUI inputs.
docs/spec/target/14_implementation_work_packages.md#11.6 requires verifying the default App first and that it does not depend on Build.
The Console renders whatever state string the BFF sends (apps/console-ui/src/components/workspaces/AgentDeliveryPanel.tsx), so an owner-attributed not-applicable state is rendered honestly.
mustStaySeparate: The BFF does not invent a CapabilityVersion or a Build for the default App; it reports those layers as not applicable and still reads Workspace and Serve facts from their owners.
The Agent combination is unchanged: when a capability version is named, the view still reads Capability and Build and still fails closed on a missing or empty owner readback.
This is a read-view composition fix; it does not deploy anything, does not change Serve's writes and does not make the BFF a writer.
minimalImplementation: When neither the current deployment nor the Workspace names a capability version, set the Capability and Build layers to a fixed `not_applicable` / `default_app_runtime_release` fact and return the Workspace and Serve facts, instead of erroring.
Add TestDeliveryViewReportsDefaultAppLayersAsNotApplicable alongside the existing Agent-view tests.
whyNotAlternative: Fabricating a placeholder version would show a Capability the owner never wrote.
Calling Capability/Build with an empty id would surface a spurious owner failure.
Refusing the view keeps the default App unusable in the Console, which is the combination Stage 6 must verify first.
